prompt: A listing broker's primary fiduciary duty to the seller client is to:

options.text: Promote the seller's interests with loyalty, care, and obedience within the law
Obtain the highest possible price even when the seller directs a quicker sale
Treat buyer and seller with equal advocacy so both receive fair representation
Advise the seller on title and tax matters as the seller's legal representative

explanation: Agency duties center on loyalty and obedience to lawful client instructions, not guaranteeing outcomes.

distractorExplanations.b: Price is not the top duty; obedience requires following the seller's lawful instruction to favor a quick sale.
distractorExplanations.c: Equal advocacy describes a neutral or dual role; a listing broker owes loyalty to the seller client, not both sides.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses agency with legal practice; a broker must refer title and tax questions to an attorney or CPA.

distractorExplanations.c: Customer status does not erase disclosure duties when agency shifts.
distractorExplanations.d: Disclosure is not optional after acceptance.

prompt: An exclusive right-to-sell listing generally means:

options.text: The listing broker is owed a commission unless the seller personally finds the buyer during the term

explanation: Exclusive right-to-sell typically protects the listing broker's commission if a sale occurs during the listing term. The exact protection follows the terms of the listing agreement.

distractorExplanations.a: That describes an exclusive agency listing, where the seller keeps the right to sell without owing a commission.
distractorExplanations.b: That describes an open listing, where only the procuring broker is paid and the seller may also sell directly.
distractorExplanations.d: That describes a net listing, which concerns how the commission is calculated, not exclusivity of the right to sell.

prompt: A net listing arrangement is often risky or restricted because

distractorExplanations.a: Reverses the entries: a credit reduces what the buyer owes, while a debit is a charge to the buyer.
distractorExplanations.c: Splits are prorations or negotiated sharing, shown as separate debits to each party, not the meaning of a debit.
distractorExplanations.d: A buyer debit is a charge to the buyer; lender-paid items appear as credits, and the loan amount is unchanged.

License discipline and civil claims

The maximum commission a broker may charge on a full-service listing agreement

At closing, along with the settlement statement
Upon the seller's written request, within ten business days

prompt: Commingling of trust funds by a New Hampshire broker typically means:

options.text: Converting trust money to the broker's own use after it is deposited
Pooling several clients' deposits in one trust account
Mixing client trust money with personal or operating funds
Depositing earnest money later than the required deposit deadline

explanation: Commingling is improper mixing of trust and personal/operating money and is a serious violation.

distractorExplanations.a: That describes conversion (misappropriation of trust money), a separate violation from commingling, which is the mixing of funds.
distractorExplanations.b: Holding many clients' deposits in a single designated trust account is permitted; commingling is mixing trust money with the broker's own funds.

prompt: If a New Hampshire listing broker and a selling broker dispute a commission, the dispute is primarily

options.text: A licensing-board matter in which the state commission orders who receives the fee
Grounds for the listing broker to hold the buyer's deposit until the fee is paid
A matter the closing agent settles by splitting the fee equally
A civil/contract matter between the brokers (or via MLS/association processes)

explanation: Commission disputes are between licensees/firms; earnest money still follows contract/escrow rules. It is not a reason to withhold a buyer's earnest money unlawfully.

distractorExplanations.a: Real estate commissions discipline licensees but do not adjudicate fee splits between brokers; that is a contract matter or association arbitration.
distractorExplanations.b: Earnest money belongs to the transaction and follows escrow rules; a broker-to-broker fee dispute is not a lawful reason to withhold it.
distractorExplanations.c: Closing agents disburse per instructions and agreements; they have no authority to resolve a commission dispute by splitting the fee.

Is granted on request to any licensee holding an active license in a bordering state

prompt: If earnest money is in dispute after a failed New Hampshire transaction, the broker should

options.text: Release it to the seller as liquidated damages

Split it evenly between buyer and seller
Apply it toward the brokerage's earned commission
